title: Symmetry testing of Boolean functions

problem.name: Symmetry testing of Boolean functions
problem.statement_latex:
\textbf{Symmetry testing of Boolean functions.} Given $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, distinguish functions depending only on Hamming weight from functions $\varepsilon$-far from every such symmetric function. Here access is by coherent membership queries.

\textbf{Symmetry testing from quantum examples.} Distinguish symmetric Boolean functions from functions $\varepsilon$-far from symmetric using copies of the uniform quantum example state; symmetry means invariance under every permutation of coordinates.

quantum.headline_latex: \textbf{Symmetry testing of Boolean functions.} $O(\varepsilon^{-1/2})$ queries by the quantum symmetry test, using the symmetric subspace and amplitude amplification.
quantum.details_latex: \textbf{Symmetry testing from quantum examples.} $O_\varepsilon(1)$ quantum examples by Caro--Naik--Slote, independent of the Boolean dimension $n$.

classical.headline_latex: \textbf{Symmetry testing of Boolean functions.} $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ membership queries by sampling pairs of inputs with equal Hamming weight and checking their values.
classical.details_latex: \textbf{Symmetry testing from quantum examples.} $\Omega(n^{1/4})$ passive uniform labeled samples are necessary at constant distance; classical tests compare sampled inputs of equal Hamming weight.
